reasoning: Observational data from authoritative climate monitoring organizations—including NOAA, the European Environment Agency (EEA), Copernicus Climate Change Service, and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)—confirm a continuous and statistically significant decline in Arctic sea ice since comprehensive satellite monitoring began in 1979. According to NOAA, summer sea ice extent has decreased by approximately 13% per decade over the 43+ year satellite record. In addition to losing total surface area in both summer and winter, the Arctic has experienced a decline in thicker, multi-year ice, leaving sea ice younger and thinner overall.
